Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY metrics.mjs stripe.mjs chart.mjs page.mjs alerts.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# MRR Pulse

After using this, you can now **see your MRR, churn and net revenue retention
from a read-only Stripe key, on a server you run**, instead of paying a metrics
service a monthly fee that grows with your revenue and sharing your customer
list with it.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/mrr-pulse/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: paste a Stripe subscription export (or load sample data)
  and get MRR, ARR, 12 months of history, logo churn, net revenue retention
  and quick ratio. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: one Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON
  file. It lists your subscriptions from Stripe every few hours, keeps the
  monthly history and serves a password-protected dashboard plus a JSON API.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | MRR Pulse |
|---|---|---|
| Stripe Dashboard Billing overview | Free, thin: no churn or retention history by month | Month-by-month new, expansion, contraction, churn, NRR |
| Baremetrics, ChartMogul, ProfitWell Metrics | Hosted; priced by revenue; your customer data lives with them | Your server, a read-only key, no fee |
| A spreadsheet fed by exports | Free, rebuilt by hand monthly; interval and quantity maths go wrong | Normalised the same way every sync |

Honest limits: only a simple run-rate projection (no seasonality or pipeline),
no multi-currency roll-up, no non-Stripe billing. It does not tell you what your churn *should* be.

## What it counts

- **MRR**: active and past-due subscriptions; every price normalised to a
  month (yearly / 12, weekly × 4.35, interval counts and seat quantities
  applied); percent-off coupons netted.
- **Not counted**: trials, paused subscriptions, metered usage, fixed-amount
  coupons. (`COUNT_PAST_DUE=false` also drops past-due.)
- **Movements**: new, expansion, contraction, churned and reactivated MRR,
  from the difference between consecutive syncs. A customer who was seen
  before and returns is *reactivation*, not *new*.
- **Rates** use the last complete month: logo churn, revenue churn, NRR, GRR,
  quick ratio ((new + expansion + reactivation) ÷ (churn + contraction)).
- **First sync is approximate.** Stripe has no price history, so the previous
  12 months are rebuilt from start and end dates at today's prices (marked `~`).
  Expansion and contraction appear from the first sync onward, which means the
  server must keep running with its state file kept to build them.
- **Retention by signup month** (dashboard and `/v1/cohorts`): of each month's
  new subscriptions, the share still active at the end of month 0, 1, 2 ...
  Logo retention is exact from start and end dates; the revenue share uses
  today's prices. Trials and paused subscriptions are left out, and a
  customer with two subscriptions counts twice.
- **MRR by plan and customer concentration** (dashboard and `/v1/plans`):
  MRR, subscriptions and share per plan (price nickname, else product id;
  seat add-ons are their own line), plus the share held by the largest and
  top five customers. Plan totals equal the headline MRR. It also reports the past-due slice
  (`atRisk`): MRR on failed payments still being retried. Customer ids are
  never shown.
- **Run-rate projection** (dashboard and `/v1/forecast?months=6`): rolls MRR
  forward using the last three complete months' pace. Base = average, low =
  worst month, high = best month. Needs two complete months; arithmetic on
  the past, not a prediction.
- **Customer concentration** (dashboard and `/v1/concentration`): the share of
  MRR held by the largest subscription, the top 5 and the top 10, with a
  low / moderate / high band (high: one subscription is 25% or more of MRR).
  Shares only, no customer or subscription ids. A customer with several
  subscriptions counts once per subscription.
- One currency per instance (`CURRENCY`, default: your most common); other
  subscriptions are left out and the dashboard says how many.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/mrr-pulse
node --test        # no network
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_live_... ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
```

Open `http://localhost:8080` and sign in with any user name and `ADMIN_KEY` as
the password. API (same key as `Authorization: Bearer ...`): `GET /v1/metrics`,
`GET /v1/months`, `GET /v1/months.csv` (the history for a spreadsheet), `GET /v1/cohorts`, `GET /v1/plans`, `GET /v1/forecast`, `GET /v1/concentration`, `POST /v1/sync`.

Stripe key: Dashboard, Developers, API keys, **Create restricted key**, set
*Subscriptions* to **Read** and everything else to None. The server only ever
issues GET requests, and the tests assert it.

Alerts (off by default): set `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` to a Slack or Discord
incoming-webhook URL (https only) and the server posts a digest (MRR, growth,
churn, NRR, quick ratio) every `DIGEST_DAYS` (default 7, `0` turns it off) and
an alert when this month's churned MRR passes `CHURN_ALERT_PCT` (default 5) of
the month's starting MRR. The webhook is yours; the message holds totals only,
no customer names or emails.

Settings: `SYNC_MINUTES` (default 360), `HISTORY_MONTHS` (12), `CURRENCY`,
`COUNT_PAST_DUE`, `MAX_PAGES` (500 pages of 100), `STATE` (path of the JSON
file; put it on a persistent disk), `PORT`.

## One-click deploy

Fork the repository, then open
`https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. Render builds the Dockerfile
in **your** account with a 1 GB disk, generates `ADMIN_KEY`, and asks for your
restricted Stripe key. Nothing runs on the author's accounts. The same
Dockerfile runs on Fly.io, Railway or any VPS.

Serve it over HTTPS only (Render does); the dashboard uses HTTP Basic auth.

## Disclaimer

No warranty; no uptime guarantee. Figures are computed from the data the API
returns and are not accounting, tax or financial advice: reconcile against your
books before using them with investors. MIT licensed. If it saves you a
subscription, you can [sponsor the author](https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood).

## Other self-deploy paths

`docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker (the command is at its top). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Both keep state on a volume and run in your own account.

docker-compose.yml.text:
# Any box with Docker:
#   ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)  docker compose up -d
# Put it behind HTTPS (Caddy, nginx, a tunnel) before real use.
services:
  mrr-pulse:
    build: .
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: ["state:/data"]
    environment:
      ADMIN_KEY: ${ADMIN_KEY:?set ADMIN_KEY}
      STATE: /data/state.json
      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}
      COMPANY_NAME: ${COMPANY_NAME:-}
      CURRENCY: ${CURRENCY:-}
volumes:
  state:

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "mrr-pulse-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Your MRR, churn and retention, from a read-only Stripe key you control

Founders pay a metrics service a monthly fee that grows with revenue to see six numbers. MRR Pulse computes them from your Stripe subscriptions: MRR and ARR, new / expansion / contraction / churned MRR, logo churn, net revenue retention and quick ratio, with a 12-month history on the first sync. Try it below on a subscription export (nothing is uploaded), then run the open-source server in your own account. No account with us, no monthly fee.

Try it on a subscription export

In Stripe: Billing → Subscriptions → Export. Needs columns for amount, interval and created; status, canceled/ended date, quantity and id are used when present. Or load made-up sample data.

MonthMRRCustomersNewChurnedNet new

History is rebuilt from start and end dates at the prices in the file, so it shows new and churned MRR only; the server adds expansion and contraction from its first sync on.

Why someone would use this

TodayCost / catch
Stripe Dashboard → Billing → OverviewFree, but a thin set of numbers and no churn or retention by month
Baremetrics, ChartMogul, ProfitWellHosted, more features, priced by revenue; your customer data lives with them
A spreadsheet fed by an exportFree, but you rebuild it by hand every month and the plan-interval maths is easy to get wrong
MRR PulseFree, MIT, read-only key, your server. Honest limits: only a simple run-rate projection, no multi-currency roll-up or other billing systems

Run it yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/fp-monorepo && cd fp-monorepo/ventures/mrr-pulse
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=rk_live_...  ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
# open http://localhost:8080 and sign in with any user name and ADMIN_KEY

The key needs Subscriptions: read and nothing else. A one-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Related tools

Same buyer, other side of churn: Dunning Engine recovers failed cards and Cancel Flow saves voluntary cancellations, and Feedback Board collects what customers ask for. Past exports can also go through the Stripe Churn Cohort Analyzer.

Questions

How is this different from Baremetrics, ChartMogul or ProfitWell?

Those are hosted services with cohorts, forecasts, integrations and support, usually priced by revenue. MRR Pulse covers the numbers most small SaaS founders check every week (MRR, ARR, new, expansion, contraction and churned MRR, logo churn, net revenue retention, quick ratio) on a server you run with a read-only key. The self-hosted server adds a retention-by-signup-month table and a simple run-rate projection (low, base, high); there is no seasonality modelling or multi-source billing.

Can it change anything in my Stripe account?

No. It only lists subscriptions, and it needs a restricted key with Subscriptions: read and nothing else. The tests assert that every request is a plain GET.

Why does the first history say it is approximate?

Stripe does not return past prices, so the first sync rebuilds the last 12 months from each subscription's start and end dates at today's price. New and churned MRR are right to within price changes; expansion and contraction only appear from the first sync onward.

What counts as MRR?

Active and past-due subscriptions, every price normalised to a month, percent-off coupons netted. Trials, paused subscriptions, metered usage and fixed-amount coupons are not counted.

Where does my Stripe key live?

In the environment of the server you deploy in your own account. The author runs nothing in between and never sees your key or your numbers.

Need recognised revenue, not just MRR? Rev Rec turns Stripe invoices into a deferred revenue schedule and journal CSV, and Trial Converter works on the trials that feed it.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. The figures are estimates computed from the data you give it; check them against your books before relying on them for investors, taxes or decisions. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# The key you paste needs Subscriptions: read and nothing else. This server never writes to Stripe.
services:
  - type: web
    name: mrr-pulse
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/mrr-pulse
    dockerfilePath: ventures/mrr-pulse/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: CURRENCY
        sync: false
